public_rationale: In a post dated January 6, 2025, Altman reported losses on OpenAI Pro subscriptions and higher usage than expected [e1]. On July 28, 2025, Anthropic described a few outlying Claude Code users as costly to support [e2]. Reporting published July 29 described weekly limits scheduled for August 28 and Anthropic's estimate that fewer than 5% of subscribers would be affected [e3]. These disclosures do not establish that either company's pre-2026 subscription terms were economically impossible to sustain at scale [e1–e3]. Altman also said he had expected the price to make money; that statement does not establish or refute the full alleged growth purpose for both companies [e4]. The claim remains unresolved [e1–e4].
limitations: The reported Pro losses lack a defined accounting basis or matched subscriber revenue and cost data [e1].
Costly outliers and projected effects of limits do not establish the economics of Anthropic's overall subscriber base [e2, e3].
The cited disclosures do not provide contemporaneous decision records establishing the full alleged purpose for both companies [e1–e4].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: It is clear that Anthropic and OpenAI both offered subscriptions that were impossible to provide at scale at the price and availability they had leading up to 2026, and did so intending to grow revenue to acquire more customers, equity investment and attention.

statement.excerpt: It’s also clear, at this point, that Anthropic and OpenAI have both offered subscriptions that were impossible to provide at scale at the price and availability that they were leading up to 2026, and that they did so with the intention of growing their revenue to acquire more customers, equity investment and attention.
statement.document_title: I Will Never Respect A Website

from_speaker: Anthropic and OpenAI have both offered subscriptions
with the intention of growing their revenue
to acquire more customers, equity investment and attention
our_interpretation: The claim concerns subscription offers made before 2026. Its starting date is unspecified, so the target period has an open start and ends on December 31, 2025.
In context, impossible to provide at scale means unable to sustain delivery economically at substantially the advertised prices and availability as the subscriber base grows.
The assertion applies to both companies and includes a separate claim about their purposes in offering those terms.
Evidence of tighter limits or losses supports concern about the terms but does not alone establish impossibility.
The wording alleges a growth purpose; it does not explicitly require proof that executives knew the offers were impossible when launched.
Leading up to 2026 is a time description, not a conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: For each company, evidence establishes the relevant pre-2026 offer, shows that its price and availability could not be sustained at scale, and connects the decision to offer those terms to the stated revenue, customer, investment, and attention objectives.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence shows that at least one company's relevant offers were economically deliverable at scale on substantially the same terms, or establishes that a material part of the attributed purpose is false.

evidence.excerpt: we are currently losing money on openai pro subscriptions!
evidence.publisher: Sam Altman, OpenAI CEO, on X
evidence.explanation: This establishes a reported loss on Pro at that time. It supplies neither a defined accounting measure nor evidence that the offer could never be sustained as costs and usage evolved.

evidence.excerpt: But a few outlying cases are very costly to support.
evidence.explanation: Anthropic acknowledges a cost problem for unusually intensive usage. It does not disclose average subscriber costs or establish that the whole subscription offering was impossible to sustain.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph; rollout timing clarified later in the article
evidence.explanation: The article reports an announcement of limits scheduled for August 28, despite its opening's past-tense wording. It also reports Anthropic's estimate that fewer than 5% of subscribers would be affected, qualifying any inference about all subscribers.

evidence.excerpt: thought we would make some money
evidence.publisher: Sam Altman, OpenAI CEO, on X
evidence.explanation: Altman says he expected the price to make money, providing an alternative to deliberate loss-leading. This self-report does not exclude simultaneous growth objectives or settle the intentions of both companies.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated pre-2026 subscription terms, usage, capacity requirements, and matched revenue and service costs for each company would establish whether those terms were sustainable at scale. Contemporaneous decision records would establish or refute the alleged revenue, customer, investment, and attention objectives.
